chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil, the companion of al-Manqari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It is sufficient honor for the believer, when he sees an evil, that Allah knows from his intention that he is displeased with it."
ai.seo_question: What is the sufficient honor for a believer when witnessing evil?
ai.summary: In the context of *Amr bil-Ma'ruf wa Nahy anil-Munkar*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation is fulfilled through sincere internal conviction (*niyyah*) when outward action is hindered by fear or inability, thereby securing the believer's honor. This aligns with the Shia scholarly distinction between the obligatory act (*wajib*) and the sufficient condition (*kafi*) for reward, emphasizing that Allah's knowledge of the heart validates the believer's status even without public declaration. It serves as a comfort to those who remain silent in the face of evil due to weakness, affirming that their inner rejection is recognized as a form of resistance.
